title: Spectrometer: compact pool-health + cost-sim UI for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Design and interactive prototype for a compact 'Spectrometer' control that surfaces GPU pool health, autoscale recommendations, and a real-time cost-simulation panel for Dedicated capacity. Aims to give ops and platform engineers a single-pane-of-glass to triage thermal/perf anomalies, tune burst settings, and preview economic impact before applying changes.
background: Current Dedicated dashboards are spread across multiple views (health timeline, capacity map, cost breakdown). Teams repeatedly request a compact control that bundles immediate signals + lightweight actuations for on-call or product platform engineers. This ticket explores a middle-ground UI: richer than a badge but lighter than a full console page.
goals: 1) Reduce time-to-decision for minor pool interventions (target < 3m). 2) Make cost impact of burst/autoscale changes immediately visible. 3) Provide safe defaults and guardrails so non-ops users can surface recommendations without risking stability.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable Spectrometer prototype in Figma with interactive cost-sim and burst knob
Design review sign-off from ENG, PM, and Security
Accessibility checklist passed for color contrast and keyboard controls
Handoff sheet with event-level telemetry requirements and front-end component spec
research_findings: Usability study (n=8 infra engineers): users prefer a single-scene immediate-action UI to switching tabs during incidents
Participants wanted a cost-preview that assumes both short burst and sustained autoscale scenarios
Confusion surfaced around 'burst cap' terminology — suggested 'Burst window' + tooltip explaining gating and safe limits
design_reviews: 2026-03-08 Review with ENG (Evan Brooks): requested clearer separation between 'recommendation' and 'user action' and instrumentation for rollbacks
2026-03-10 Design critique with PM (Lena Morris): asked for explicit SLA-risk indicator tied to SLO calc in console-telemetry
2026-03-12 Security check (Anika Rao): asked that auditing metadata (who toggled, old vs new values) be persisted to audit logs before rollout
decisions: Keep Spectrometer as an embeddable canvas (can live on pool overview and on-call quick panel)
Cost simulation runs on a 1-minute sampled model; results are approximate and surfaced with a confidence badge
Default safe burst cap = 20% of reserved capacity; can be raised by users with 'ops' role after confirmation
tradeoffs: Embedding cost-sim client-side reduces round trips but requires approximate models and clear UX about uncertainty
Showing per-GPU thermals at high fidelity increases telemetry costs — compromise: provide per-node sparklines and a detailed drill-in for engineers
Immediate actuations (burst toggle) are fast but risk operator error; we add a two-step confirmation and audit log integration
accessibility_notes: Ensure spectrogram heatmap has non-color encodings (pattern overlay + numeric tooltips)
Keyboard focus order defined for all interactive elements (burst knob, simulate slider, apply button)
Contrast ratios validated to WCAG AA for primary control palette
